title: LLM inference metric synthesis proxy
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a lightweight metric synthesis proxy (MSP) that receives OTel metric streams from inference hosts and emits a consolidated, cost-aware set of Prometheus-style time series and KPI envelopes for downstream SLO/alerting and Console dashboards. The MSP’s role is to: 1) translate OTel/SDK host metrics into tenant-aware inference KPIs (per-model latency P50/P95/P99, per-request token counts, kv-cache hit/miss, batching sizes), 2) reduce cardinality via deterministic bucketing and dimension collapsing, 3) maintain exemplar links back to traces/span IDs for latency/error correlation, and 4) provide a config surface for per-customer aggregation policies and retention. This ticket covers the initial MVP proxy implementation, schema mapping, and rollout plan to a subset of tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OTLP gRPC/HTTP metric streams and authenticates via service token
Generates a normalized Prometheus-compatible metric feed (Pushgateway-compatible or remote write shim) with tenant/model labels limited to configured cardinality
Produces configured buckets for sequence-length and inference-latency histograms that align with Console percentiles
Attaches exemplar metadata (trace_id/span_id) for top latency/error samples to enable trace correlation in Console
Provides a feature flag to enable per-tenant aggregation policy and the ability to fallback to raw metrics for enterprise tenants
End-to-end tests validate correctness vs. golden traces/metrics harness and integration smoke test with metrics-collector (dev environment)
comments: 2026-02-27 - Ava Chen: Kickoff — collected requirements from PM and Console team. Primary ask: reduce cardinality while preserving debugability for P0 tenant incidents. Draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Metric+Synthesis+Proxy+Design

2026-03-02 - Miguel Ortiz: Prototype a simple OTLP receiver using existing otel-collector components. Initial approach: use an otel filter + custom processor to remap labels, then export via remote_write. Prototype validated in local cluster with synthetic traffic.
2026-03-05 - Review (PM): Sarah Li requested explicit support for per-model variant labels and a global 'model_family' collapse rule to avoid explosion when customers use dynamically-named variants.

2026-03-07 - Design decision: Use deterministic bucketing for sequence_length and latency (power-of-two for sequence, fixed SLO-driven latency buckets) to normalize histograms across hosts. Trade-off: some loss of granularity for tail debugging but significant reduction in series cardinality.

2026-03-09 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/412 — initial otel processor + prometheus remote_write shim. Miguel assigned as reviewer. Includes unit tests for label collapse logic.

2026-03-11 - Security review: flagged need to ensure trace_id propagation does not leak customer PII. Security suggested strict exemplar sampling policy and masking of user identifiers in labels. Added security_review_required = true.

2026-03-12 - QA notes: found edge-case where ephemeral model_id labels from A/B rollout created >10k series in staging for a high-churn tenant. Mitigation: add per-tenant maximum-label-count and a fallback 'model_summary' label that groups low-volume variants into 'others'.

2026-03-13 - Next steps: finalize config API for tenant policies, add integration test with Console percentile computation, schedule canary rollout to 5 tenants (low-risk then medium-high). Owner: Miguel Ortiz. Oncall notified of canary windows.
notes: Implementation choices: prefer in-cluster MSP as a sidecar/daemonset to avoid cross-AZ egress. Keep CPU/memory footprint minimal by using streaming processors and bounded buffers. Consider leveraging existing collector extensions for export resiliency and backpressure. TODO: benchmark throughput vs. current metric pipeline under 100k rps simulated workload.
